name: Unattributed
note: Provenance not established. Every file here is on Maki's 15×15 grid and carries NO CC0 metadata stamp — see icons/versatiles/source.json for what that stamp means.

whatIsKnown.authoringGrid: Coordinates are natively grid-aligned on the 15-unit canvas — 32% integers, 12% half-steps, 49% landing on quarter-units, and 100% at two decimal places or fewer. That is the profile of icons DRAWN at 15×15, not of artwork rescaled from a larger canvas.
whatIsKnown.exportStyle: Compact absolute path data with no separator after the command letter (`M2 3C2 1.9 2.9 1 4 1L11 1`), rounded to two decimals. Byte-for-byte the same export style Temaki uses.
whatIsKnown.notTheNounProject: Investigated and rejected. The Noun Project publishes on a 100×100 canvas and almost entirely under CC BY rather than CC0. A 100→15 rescale would leave coordinates clustered on 0.15 multiples and would not produce quarter-unit alignment; neither signature is present. Nothing here shows any trace of a rescale.

ruledOutAsVerbatimCopies.method: Exact path geometry against 1033 distinct upstream geometries, then visual overlap (IoU on 32×32 rasters), then a longest-shared-substring test over the raw path data.
ruledOutAsVerbatimCopies.caveat: Exact-match alone gives FALSE NEGATIVES for edited icons. The substring test found two derivatives that exact matching missed: bus (192 identical characters) and tram (363) were Temaki icons with one detail redrawn, and have been moved to icons/temaki/. Use the substring test, not equality, before concluding anything here is original.

leads.lead: Arrived in commit 5454666 (2026-07-04), a batch of 23 replacements that swapped artwork and dropped the CC0 stamp. Other icons from that same batch — police_officer, seesaw, and now tram — trace to Temaki, so the batch drew on Temaki even where these nine do not match it.
Predate that batch. arrow2 and arrow3 are 16×16, unlike everything else here. star_of_david is a hollow hexagram where maki/religious-jewish is solid — deliberately different, not a copy.

howToResolve: Best remaining explanation is that these were drawn for VersaTiles in Temaki's style and simply never stamped — the versatiles-sprites repo they came through is deleted from GitHub, so that cannot be confirmed from here. `npm run icons-report` lists what is here; move a file into its source folder once identified and update its sprite entry in scripts/config-sprites.ts.
